title: Write an operational definition — TB sputum turnaround
brief:
The PHC clinic's QI team has chosen a new process measure: **proportion of TB-suspect outpatients who receive a sputum smear microscopy result within 48 hours of sample submission**.

Before data collection begins, the team needs a written operational definition that any two nurses at this clinic could read and use to count the same way.

task.stem: Write a complete operational definition for this measure.
task.context:
**Measure:** Proportion of TB-suspect outpatients with sputum smear microscopy result within 48 hours of sample submission.

**Setting:** District-level PHC clinic. Sputum samples are logged in a paper TB laboratory register and sent to the district lab. Results are phoned back to the clinic and recorded in the same register.
task.placeholder:
Write your operational definition here. Aim to include: numerator, denominator, inclusions, exclusions, data source, and measurement window.

Example format:
Numerator: ...
Denominator: ...
Inclusions: ...
Exclusions: ...
Data source: ...
Measurement window: ...

rubric.label: Numerator — counts the desired event
rubric.hint: Should describe TB-suspect patients whose result was received AND recorded within 48 hours of sample submission.

rubric.label: Denominator — defines the eligible population
rubric.hint: Should identify all TB-suspect outpatients who submitted a sputum sample in the period — regardless of whether the result arrived in time.

rubric.label: Inclusions — explicitly names who or what is in scope
rubric.hint: e.g., includes first-episode and retreatment suspects; includes samples taken on repeat visits.

rubric.label: Exclusions — explicitly names who or what is out of scope
rubric.hint: e.g., excludes samples where the lab register shows the sample was rejected or lost in transit.

rubric.label: Data source — a named record or system
rubric.hint: Should name the specific document or system — e.g., paper TB laboratory register, DHIS2 TB module, clinic referral logbook.

debrief.correct: A strong operational definition names all six components: **numerator** (who was counted as timely), **denominator** (all eligible patients submitted), **inclusions** (who is in scope), **exclusions** (who is out of scope), **data source** (the named register or system), and **measurement window** (the review period). With all six specified, two data collectors at different clinics should reach the same count from the same register.
debrief.wrong: Check that your definition addresses all six components. The most common gaps: writing the numerator as 'patients with a result' without specifying the 48-hour cut-off; omitting exclusions entirely; naming a vague data source like 'the register' without specifying *which* register; and forgetting the measurement window. Re-read the debrief rubric and try again.
debrief.rule_cited: Operational definitions — six components: numerator, denominator, inclusions, exclusions, data source, measurement window. Provost & Murray ch. 3; IHI QI 102.
